chunks: Draw an H-bridge circuit. The question: Draw an H-bidge circuit.
An H-bridge is two legs side by side, drawn like the letter H.
Each leg has a high-side switch from the supply down to a middle node, and a low-side switch from that node to ground.
The motor sits between the two middle nodes, as the crossbar of the H.
A good drawing also shows the transistors (usually MOSFETs), their built-in diodes, and the gate drivers that switch them.
Picture a canal with four gates, two on each side, and a channel across the middle that holds a paddle wheel.
Open the top-left and bottom-right gates, and water flows across the channel one way. Open the top-right and bottom-left gates, and it flows the other way, so the wheel reverses.
Open both gates on the same side and the water rushes straight from supply to drain without touching the wheel.
The H. S1/S3 form the left leg (midpoint A) and S2/S4 the right leg (midpoint B). The motor is the crossbar.
Closing S1 and S4 puts A at V M and B at ground; closing S2 and S3 does the opposite.
Node: a connection point in a circuit. Leg (half-bridge): one high-side and one low-side switch in series, with the output at the midpoint.
Body diode: the diode built into every MOSFET. It gives the motor's current a path when switches turn off.
Shoot-through: both switches in one leg on at once, which shorts the supply. Dead time: a brief gap with both switches of a leg off, between transitions.
Label the switches S1 (top left), S2 (top right), S3 (bottom left), and S4 (bottom right), with 12 volts as the supply.
S1 and S4 on puts the left node at 12 volts and the right at 0 volts, so the motor gets +12 volts. S2 and S3 on reverses it to minus 12 volts.
Both low sides on, S3 and S4, shorts the motor to brake it. All off, it coasts. S1 and S3 together is the forbidden short.
For real parts, add body diodes and gate drivers with dead time. That is the whole idea.
"An H-bridge is two half-bridges: each leg has a high-side and a low-side switch, and the motor sits between the two middle nodes.
Turn on top-left plus bottom-right and current flows one way; top-right plus bottom-left reverses it; both low sides shorts the motor for braking; all off lets it coast.
With MOSFETs I draw NFETs low and PFETs, or bootstrapped NFETs, high, include the body diodes for the inductive freewheel path, and add gate drivers with dead time so one leg never shoots through."
Quick check.
In an H-bridge with high-side switches S1 (left), S2 (right) and low-side S3 (left), S4 (right), which pair do you close to drive current through the motor from the left node to the right node?
